snippet.title: San Diego Surprised Us — Best Hidden Gems, Food & Views in 48 Hours
snippet.description:
We spent 48 hours in San Diego and honestly? It completely won us over. From artsy neighbourhoods and insane food markets to wild sea lions and jaw-dropping coastal cliffs — San Diego is one of those cities that delivers way more than you expect.
Whether you're planning a San Diego trip, a California road trip, or you're a digital nomad scoping out your next base — this San Diego travel guide covers everything you need to know before you go.
In this video, we take you through the best things to do in San Diego in 48 hours, including spots that most tourists miss entirely.

Here's a taste of what we explore:
🌿 A dreamy matcha café in North Park that's equal parts aesthetic and delicious
🍳 A breakfast spot serving some of the most creative, flavour-packed plates in the city
🛍️ A design store in North Park that will make you want to redecorate your entire life
🌴 A hidden tropical canyon inside Balboa Park — bigger than Central Park and Chicago's Millennium Park combined
🦭 La Jolla Cove's wild sea lion colony — one of the most incredible free experiences in all of California
🌅 Sunset Cliffs — the most serene stretch of coastline you've never heard of
🍝 Dinner in Little Italy with full-bodied sangria and pasta that hits different after a full day of exploring

San Diego has a neighbourhood for every type of traveller. North Park is perfect for foodies and creatives, Balboa Park is a must for nature lovers and culture seekers, and La Jolla is an absolute non-negotiable — especially if you love animals. We also stop by Liberty Public Market, Seaport Village, and more.
This is not your average tourist itinerary. We show you the real San Diego — the flavours, the neighbourhoods, the hidden corners, and the moments that made us say "we're coming back."

snippet.description:
Welcome to a brand new series on the channel! You've seen X, working alongside me on our projects. Now, it's time for her to take the lead in her very own show: Farm Secrets with X!

Join us for the very first episode as X takes on the mission of building our dream permaculture farm here in Thailand, starting with one of the most beautiful and symbolic flowers—the lotus.
In this video, X's journey begins in a neighbor's field, wading through the mud to gather the perfect red lotus plants. She’ll share her secrets on how to plant them in our lake, care for them so they thrive, and explain the vital role they play in our permaculture farm's ecosystem.

You'll also get a little tour of the farm and meet some of our adorable residents, including the baby ducks, turkeys and cats!

This series is more than just about farming; it's about a new beginning and building a sustainable paradise from the ground up. It's a journey of beauty, peace, and abundance, and we're so excited to share it all with you, with X as our guide.

snippet.title: Thai-Cambodia War Reaches My Village | A Fragile Ceasefire?
snippet.description:
Thank you to those who offered to help out. I will leave X's PayPal link for as long as the people are staying here. All donations will go towards food, clothing and other supplies, to various evacuation centres in Sisaket Province.

PalPal Donations: https://paypal.me/NKaewmontri

In the wake of intense border clashes, a fragile ceasefire between Thailand and Cambodia has been announced following crucial negotiations. But what does this mean for the families caught in the middle? In this video, we go beyond the headlines to the human heart of the conflict, sharing a firsthand look inside an evacuation center in Sisaket province, Thailand, just miles from the border.

This is not our usual content. We are a small farm focused on permaculture and sharing Thai culture. However, when the conflict escalated, the consequences arrived on our doorstep. We felt compelled to document the reality for the people whose lives have been upended and show the incredible resilience of the human spirit.

Our journey takes you with us as we witness the direct impact of the Thailand-Cambodia border situation. We visit a local temple that has been transformed into a sanctuary for hundreds of evacuees—families, children, and the elderly who were forced to flee their homes with little more than what they could carry. snippet.title: Why Do Old Men Love Thailand? 🇹🇭
snippet.description:
So, why do old men love Thailand?

Before we dive into that minefield, a quick word from our sponsor: me! I’ve launched a Patreon page:

https://patreon.com/FarangFarm

It’s a backstage pass to the unglazed, slightly unhinged process behind these films. If you want to become a founding member, get your name in the credits, access the jokes that were too dark for the final cut, and vote on future misadventures.

Awkward part over.

This film started as a simple "day in the life" but quickly spiralled into a meditation on, well, everything. We begin with the organised chaos of the rice harvest. A frantic, beautiful race against time and weather, fuelled by diesel fumes and a questionable approach to health and safety regulations. You’ll get a first-person view from atop a moving rice harvester, a vantage point that offers spectacular views and near-death experiences.

As day turns to night, the story shifts from the cycle of labour to the cycle of life itself. We join a mission to honour a beloved family member who recently passed away. This involves a journey deep into the heart of Isaan's legendary Morlam music scene, gate-crashing a local concert on a quest to book the perfect band for a final, glorious send-off party. It's here that we explore the beautiful Thai philosophy of 'Kon la Thanon', the idea that each of us walks our own unique road, in this life and the next.

Finally, we return to the central, awkward question. I take an honest look at the one, maybe two, stereotypes of the Western man living in Thailand.

But as is so often the case, the cliché is just the surface. We return to the farm to find an unexpected and quiet miracle: a colony of butterflies, thriving in the leaves of a banana plant I was told I should have managed better.

Maybe the real reason people fall in love with this place isn't about escaping an end, but about finding a place where you are constantly reminded that you are, for better or worse, still profoundly, thrillingly, alive. For a while, at least.

Thanks for being here. Every comment is read and appreciated. PLease share your own unique stories.

You were told the Philippines was easy.
Cheap. Simple. A place where Western men could start over.

This video shows you the reality.

Men don’t fail in the Philippines because they’re unlucky.
They fail because they come in the wrong order — chasing lifestyle and dating before they secure stability, legality, and runway.

A few thousand dollars saved.
No real plan.
No exit strategy.

This video breaks down why Western men fail in the Philippines, how money quietly becomes expected, how dating turns into a liability, and why once your finances run wrong here, there is no reset button.

This is not about blaming the country.
This is not about blaming women.

It’s about order, math, and survival.

If you’re already here — understand this before it’s too late.

• When money becomes expected instead of optional
• The moment exits disappear

This is survival math.

snippet.title: Work Around Visa Thailand Possiblities
snippet.description:
The best option depends on how you plan to work in Thailand. Here are the main legal pathways:

Working for a Thai employer (most common)
Obtain a Non-Immigrant B (Business) visa.
Your employer sponsors your application and arranges a Thai work permit.
You generally need both the visa and the work permit before you can legally work.
Remote work for a foreign employer or your own overseas business
The Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) is intended for digital nomads and remote workers.
If you meet the eligibility requirements, it allows longer stays while working remotely for clients or employers outside Thailand.
Long-Term Resident (LTR) Visa
Designed for higher-income professionals, investors, and certain remote workers.
It offers long-term residence and additional benefits if you satisfy the financial and employment requirements.
SMART Visa
Available for professionals, executives, entrepreneurs, and investors in targeted industries.
Eligibility is more specialized but can provide work authorization with fewer administrative steps.
Teaching English
Many foreigners work in schools after securing a teaching position.
The school typically sponsors the work visa and work permit. A bachelor's degree is commonly required, and a TEFL certificate is often preferred.

If your goal is to train Muay Thai in Koh Samui while earning money, common legal approaches include:

Working remotely for a foreign company under a visa that permits your situation (such as the DTV if you qualify).
Finding a Thai employer willing to sponsor a work visa.
Teaching English or another specialized skill through a sponsoring employer.

A variety of plans from basic to comprehensive, with annual benefit limits up to several million USD/THB depending on the tier.

Inpatient coverage for hospital stays, surgeries, diagnostics, and treatment costs.

Outpatient benefits and maternity care on many plans (e.g., Standard, Comprehensive).

Cashless direct billing at a large network of hospitals in Thailand and ASEAN to minimize upfront costs.

Emergency medical and evacuation coverage including worldwide emergency treatment.

Pre‑existing conditions coverage available under specialized Expat Care plans after a waiting period.

Lifetime renewability with no age limit on many plans.

🌏 Travel & Visa Insurance

Plans for short trips (e.g., Bon Voyage Single‑Trip) and annual coverage for frequent travelers.

Long‑stay/visa compliant policies that meet Thailand’s minimum health insurance requirements for certain visa types.
